sanskrit: indreṇa sahitaṃ yasya havir āgrayaṇaṃ smṛtam agnir āgrayaṇo nāma bhānor evānvayas tu saḥ
english: That fire whose oblation offered together with Indra is known as the āgrayaṇa — that fire is called Āgrayaṇa, and he too is a descendant of Bhānu.

sanskrit: cāturmāsyeṣu nityānāṃ haviṣāṃ yo niragrahaḥ caturbhiḥ sahitaḥ putrair bhānor evānvayas tu saḥ
english: That fire which, in the cāturmāsya rites, receives the regular oblations without interruption, accompanied by four sons — he too is a descendant of Bhānu.

sanskrit: niśāṃ tv ajanayat kanyām agnīṣomāv ubhau tathā manor evābhavad bhāryā suṣuve pañca pāvakān
english: Night herself bore a daughter, and both Agni and Soma likewise; she who had been Manu's wife gave birth to five purifying fires.

sanskrit: pūjyate haviṣāgryeṇa cāturmāsyeṣu pāvakaḥ parjanyasahitaḥ śrīmān agnir vaiśvānaras tu saḥ
english: That fire who is worshipped with the choicest oblations in the cāturmāsya ceremonies, the glorious one who acts together with Parjanya — he is known as Vaiśvānara.

sanskrit: asya lokasya sarvasya yaḥ patiḥ paripaṭhyate so 'gnir viśvapatir nāma dvitīyo vai manoḥ sutaḥ tataḥ sviṣṭaṃ bhaved ājyaṃ sviṣṭakṛt paramaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: That fire who is celebrated as the lord of this entire world is named Viśvapati, the second son of Manu; through him the offered ghee becomes truly well-offered, and he is accordingly called Sviṣṭakṛt, the supreme maker of perfect sacrifice.

sanskrit: kanyā sā rohiṇī nāma hiraṇyakaśipoḥ sutā karmaṇāsau babhau bhāryā sa vahniḥ sa prajāpatiḥ
english: That maiden called Rohiṇī, daughter of Hiraṇyakaśipu, became his wife by his own action; that fire is also a Prajāpati.

sanskrit: prāṇam āśritya yo dehaṃ pravartayati dehinām tasya saṃnihito nāma śabdarūpasya sādhanaḥ
english: That fire who, abiding in the vital breath, sustains the bodies of embodied beings — he is named Saṃnihita, the accomplisher of sound and form.

sanskrit: śuklakṛṣṇagatir devo yo bibharti hutāśanam akalmaṣaḥ kalmaṣāṇāṃ kartā krodhāśritas tu saḥ
english: That deity who moves along both the bright and dark paths and sustains the fire of oblation — he is himself without blemish yet is the cause of impurities in others, and he abides in wrath.

sanskrit: kapilaṃ paramarṣiṃ ca yaṃ prāhur yatayaḥ sadā agniḥ sa kapilo nāma sāṃkhyayogapravartakaḥ
english: That fire whom ascetics always proclaim as the great sage Kapila — he is named Kapila, the inaugurator of the Sāṃkhya yoga.

sanskrit: agnir yacchati bhūtāni yena bhūtāni nityadā karmasv iha vicitreṣu so 'graṇīr vahnir ucyate
english: That fire by whom beings are constantly set in motion among the varied activities of this world — he is called Agraṇī, the foremost fire.

sanskrit: imān anyān samasṛjat pāvakān prathitān bhuvi agnihotrasya duṣṭasya prāyaścittārtham ulbaṇān
english: He created these and other well-known purifying fires on earth — fierce ones, meant as expiations for the defiled agnihotra.

sanskrit: saṃspṛśeyur yadānyonyaṃ kathaṃ cid vāyunāgnayaḥ iṣṭir aṣṭākapālena kāryā vai śucaye 'gnaye
english: If the fires should somehow come into contact with one another through the wind, an eight-potsherd iṣṭi offering must be performed for the fire called Śuci.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāgnir yadā dvābhyāṃ saṃsṛjeta tadā kila iṣṭir aṣṭākapālena kāryā vai vītaye 'gnaye
english: If the southern fire should become commingled with the other two, then an eight-potsherd iṣṭi offering must be performed for the fire called Vīta.

sanskrit: yady agnayo hi spṛśyeyur niveśasthā davāgninā iṣṭir aṣṭākapālena kāryā tu śucaye 'gnaye
english: If the sacred fires kept in the household should be touched by a forest fire, an eight-potsherd iṣṭi offering must be performed for the fire called Śuci.

sanskrit: agniṃ rajasvalā cet strī saṃspṛśed agnihotrikam iṣṭir aṣṭākapālena kāryā dasyumate 'gnaye
english: If a woman in her impure state should touch the agnihotra fire, an eight-potsherd iṣṭi offering must be performed for the fire called Dasyumant.

sanskrit: mṛtaḥ śrūyeta yo jīvan pareyuḥ paśavo yathā iṣṭir aṣṭākapālena kartavyābhimate 'gnaye
english: If someone who was reported dead is heard to be alive, or if livestock perish, an eight-potsherd iṣṭi offering must be performed for the fire called Abhimata.

sanskrit: ārto na juhuyād agniṃ trirātraṃ yas tu brāhmaṇaḥ iṣṭir aṣṭākapālena kāryā syād uttarāgnaye
english: If a brahmin who is afflicted fails to offer into the fire for three nights, an eight-potsherd iṣṭi offering must be performed for the fire called Uttarāgni.

sanskrit: darśaṃ ca paurṇamāsaṃ ca yasya tiṣṭhet pratiṣṭhitam iṣṭir aṣṭākapālena kāryā pathikṛte 'gnaye
english: If the new-moon and full-moon observances remain established but are neglected, an eight-potsherd iṣṭi offering must be performed for the fire called Pathikṛt.

sanskrit: sūtikāgnir yadā cāgniṃ saṃspṛśed agnihotrikam iṣṭir aṣṭākapālena kāryā cāgnimate 'gnaye
english: If the fire of the birthing chamber should touch the agnihotra fire, an eight-potsherd iṣṭi offering must be performed for the fire called Agnimant.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca āpasya muditā bhāryā sahasya paramā priyā bhūpatir bhuvabhartā ca janayat pāvakaṃ param
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: The joyful wife of Āpa and the most beloved wife of Saha — together with Bhūpati and Bhuvabhartā — gave birth to the supreme purifying fire.

sanskrit: bhūtānāṃ cāpi sarveṣāṃ yaṃ prāhuḥ pāvakaṃ patim ātmā bhuvanabharteti sānvayeṣu dvijātiṣu
english: Him whom they call the lord and purifier of all beings, the self and sustainer of the world — so he is proclaimed among twice-born men with their lineages.

sanskrit: mahatāṃ caiva bhūtānāṃ sarveṣām iha yaḥ patiḥ bhagavān sa mahātejā nityaṃ carati pāvakaḥ
english: He who is the lord of all great beings in this world — that blessed, supremely radiant purifying fire moves perpetually through all things.

sanskrit: agnir gṛhapatir nāma nityaṃ yajñeṣu pūjyate hutaṃ vahati yo havyam asya lokasya pāvakaḥ
english: The fire named Gṛhapati is perpetually worshipped in sacrificial rites; he it is who carries the oblations that are offered — the purifier of this world.

sanskrit: apāṃ garbho mahābhāgaḥ sahaputro mahādbhutaḥ bhūpatir bhuvabhartā ca mahataḥ patir ucyate
english: The glorious embryo of the waters, the wondrous son of Saha, Bhūpati, and Bhuvabhartā — he is called the lord of the great.

sanskrit: dahan mṛtāni bhūtāni tasyāgnir bharato 'bhavat agniṣṭome ca niyataḥ kratuśreṣṭho bharasya tu
english: Burning the dead bodies of beings, Bharata became his fire; and in the agniṣṭoma rite, ordained as the foremost of sacrifices, he is the fire of Bharata.

sanskrit: āyāntaṃ niyataṃ dṛṣṭvā praviveśārṇavaṃ bhayāt devās taṃ nādhigacchanti mārgamāṇā yathādiśam
english: Seeing one who was surely coming toward them, fire hid himself in the ocean out of fear; the gods could not find him though they searched in every direction.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tv agnir atharvāṇaṃ tato vacanam abravīt devānāṃ vaha havyaṃ tvam ahaṃ vīra sudurbalaḥ atharvan gaccha madhvakṣaṃ priyam etat kuruṣva me
english: But when fire saw Atharvan, he then spoke these words: "O hero, carry the oblations of the gods yourself — I am extremely weak. O Atharvan, go to the sweet-eyed one; do me this favour."

sanskrit: preṣya cāgnir atharvāṇam anyaṃ deśaṃ tato 'gamat matsyās tasya samācakhyuḥ kruddhas tān agnir abravīt
english: Having sent Atharvan away, fire then departed to another region; but the fish reported his whereabouts. Angered, fire spoke to them.

sanskrit: bhakṣyā vai vividhair bhāvair bhaviṣyatha śarīriṇām atharvāṇaṃ tathā cāpi havyavāho 'bravīd vacaḥ
english: "You shall become food for embodied beings in many ways and conditions!" — thus fire the oblation-carrier also spoke his words to Atharvan.

sanskrit: anunīyamāno 'pi bhṛśaṃ devavākyād dhi tena saḥ naicchad voḍhuṃ haviḥ sarvaṃ śarīraṃ ca samatyajat
english: Though greatly entreated by him with the words of the gods, fire still refused to carry all the oblations and abandoned his body entirely.

sanskrit: sa tac charīraṃ saṃtyajya praviveśa dharāṃ tadā bhūmiṃ spṛṣṭvāsṛjad dhātūn pṛthak pṛthag atīva hi
english: Having cast off that body, he then entered the earth; and upon touching the ground he released the various minerals, one by one, in great profusion.

sanskrit: āsyāt sugandhi tejaś ca asthibhyo devadāru ca śleṣmaṇaḥ sphaṭikaṃ tasya pittān marakataṃ tathā
english: From his mouth came fragrant radiance and from his bones came the deva-dāru tree; from his phlegm came crystal, and from his bile came the emerald.

sanskrit: yakṛt kṛṣṇāyasaṃ tasya tribhir eva babhuḥ prajāḥ nakhās tasyābhrapaṭalaṃ śirājālāni vidrumam śarīrād vividhāś cānye dhātavo 'syābhavan nṛpa
english: From his liver came black iron; through him three classes of creatures came into being; from his nails came layers of cloud, from his network of veins came coral, and from his body came many other diverse minerals, O king.

sanskrit: evaṃ tyaktvā śarīraṃ tu parame tapasi sthitaḥ bhṛgvaṅgirādibhir bhūyas tapasotthāpitas tadā
english: Having thus abandoned his body and remaining in supreme austerity, he was once again raised up from his penance by Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, and the others.

sanskrit: bhṛśaṃ jajvāla tejasvī tapasāpyāyitaḥ śikhī dṛṣṭvā ṛṣīn bhayāc cāpi praviveśa mahārṇavam
english: Blazing intensely, his flame nourished and swelled by austerity, he saw the sages and from fear entered the great ocean once more.

sanskrit: tasmin naṣṭe jagad bhītam atharvāṇam athāśritam arcayām āsur evainam atharvāṇaṃ surarṣayaḥ
english: When he had vanished, the world was seized with fear and took refuge in Atharvan; the divine sages then worshipped Atharvan himself.

sanskrit: atharvā tv asṛjal lokān ātmanālokya pāvakam miṣatāṃ sarvabhūtānām unmamātha mahārṇavam
english: Then Atharvan, perceiving fire within himself, created the worlds, and before the eyes of all beings he churned up the great ocean.

sanskrit: evam agnir bhagavatā naṣṭaḥ pūrvam atharvaṇā āhūtaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ havyaṃ vahati sarvadā
english: Thus fire, who had previously vanished, was called back by the blessed Atharvan, and henceforth he forever carries the oblations for all beings.

sanskrit: evaṃ tv ajanayad dhiṣṇyān vedoktān vibudhān bahūn vicaran vividhān deśān bhramamāṇas tu tatra vai
english: And so, wandering and roaming through many and various lands, he fathered the divine fire-altars — many wise ones as declared in the Vedas.

sanskrit: sindhuvarjaṃ pañca nadyo devikātha sarasvatī gaṅgā ca śatakumbhā ca śarayūr gaṇḍasāhvayā
english: Excluding the Sindhu, five rivers — Devikā, Sarasvatī, Gaṅgā, Śatakumbhā, Śarayū, and the one called Gaṇḍa —

sanskrit: carmaṇvatī mahī caiva medhyā medhātithis tathā tāmrāvatī vetravatī nadyas tisro 'tha kauśikī
english: Carmaṇvatī, Mahī, Medhyā, Medhātithi, Tāmrāvatī, Vetravatī, those three rivers, and Kauśikī —

sanskrit: tamasā narmadā caiva nadī godāvarī tathā veṇṇā praveṇī bhīmā ca medrathā caiva bhārata
english: Tamasā, Narmadā, the river Godāvarī, Veṇṇā, Praveṇī, Bhīmā, and Medrathā, O Bhārata —

sanskrit: bhāratī suprayogā ca kāverī murmurā tathā kṛṣṇā ca kṛṣṇaveṇṇā ca kapilā śoṇa eva ca etā nadyas tu dhiṣṇyānāṃ mātaro yāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
english: Bhāratī, Suprayogā, Kāverī, Murmurā, Kṛṣṇā, Kṛṣṇaveṇṇā, Kapilā, and Śoṇa — these rivers, which are proclaimed, are the mothers of the fire-altars.

sanskrit: adbhutasya priyā bhāryā tasyāḥ putro viḍūrathaḥ yāvantaḥ pāvakāḥ proktāḥ somās tāvanta eva ca
english: The beloved wife of Adbhuta bore a son named Viḍūratha; and as many purifying fires as have been named, so many somas there are as well.

sanskrit: atreś cāpy anvaye jātā brahmaṇo mānasāḥ prajāḥ atriḥ putrān sraṣṭukāmas tān evātmany adhārayat tasya tad brahmaṇaḥ kāyān nirharanti hutāśanāḥ
english: The mind-born offspring of Brahman were also born in the lineage of Atri; Atri, wishing to create sons, held them within himself, and the oblation-carrying fires draw them forth from the bodies of that brahmic power.

sanskrit: evam ete mahātmānaḥ kīrtitās te 'gnayo mayā aprameyā yathotpannāḥ śrīmantas timirāpahāḥ
english: Thus have I recounted these great-souled fires to you — immeasurable in their origins, glorious, destroyers of darkness.

sanskrit: adbhutasya tu māhātmyaṃ yathā vedeṣu kīrtitam tādṛśaṃ viddhi sarveṣām eko hy eṣa hutāśanaḥ
english: Know that the greatness of Adbhuta, as it is celebrated in the Vedas, is that of all of them together — for this oblation-carrier is truly the one fire.

sanskrit: eka evaiṣa bhagavān vijñeyaḥ prathamo 'ṅgirāḥ bahudhā niḥsṛtaḥ kāyāj jyotiṣṭomaḥ kratur yathā
english: This blessed one is to be known as one alone — the primeval Aṅgiras; he has issued forth in manifold forms from his body, just as the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice does from its single rite.

sanskrit: ity eṣa vaṃśaḥ sumahān agnīnāṃ kīrtito mayā pāvito vividhair mantrair havyaṃ vahati dehinām
english: Thus this supremely great lineage of fires has been recounted by me; purified by various sacred formulas, he carries the oblations for all embodied beings.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca agnīnāṃ vividho vaṃśaḥ kīrtitas te mayānagha śṛṇu janma tu kauravya kārttikeyasya dhīmataḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: The manifold lineage of fires has been recounted to you by me, O sinless one. Now hear, O Kauravya, the birth of the wise Kārttikeya.

sanskrit: adbhutasyādbhutaṃ putraṃ pravakṣyāmy amitaujasam jātaṃ saptarṣibhāryābhir brahmaṇyaṃ kīrtivardhanam
english: I shall tell of the wondrous son of Adbhuta — of immeasurable might, born through the wives of the Seven Sages, devoted to brahmin virtues, and the increaser of glory.

sanskrit: devāsurāḥ purā yattā vinighnantaḥ parasparam tatrājayan sadā devān dānavā ghorarūpiṇaḥ
english: In former times, gods and demons were constantly engaged in slaying one another; and in those battles the fearsome-formed dānavas always conquered the gods.

sanskrit: vadhyamānaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā bahuśas taiḥ puraṃdaraḥ svasainyanāyakārthāya cintām āpa bhṛśaṃ tadā
english: Seeing his forces repeatedly slaughtered by them, Puraṃdara fell into deep anxiety as to how he might find a leader for his own army.

sanskrit: devasenāṃ dānavair yo bhagnāṃ dṛṣṭvā mahābalaḥ pālayed vīryam āśritya sa jñeyaḥ puruṣo mayā
english: "That supremely mighty man who, seeing the divine army broken by the demons, would protect it by relying on his own valour — he is the one I must find."

sanskrit: sa śailaṃ mānasaṃ gatvā dhyāyann artham imaṃ bhṛśam śuśrāvārtasvaraṃ ghoram atha muktaṃ striyā tadā
english: Going to the Mānasa mountain and brooding deeply on this matter, he then heard a terrible cry of distress that had been let out by a woman.

sanskrit: abhidhāvatu mā kaś cit puruṣas trātu caiva ha patiṃ ca me pradiśatu svayaṃ vā patir astu me
english: "Let some man come running to me! Let him rescue me! Let him point out a husband for me, or let him become my husband himself!"

sanskrit: puraṃdaras tu tām āha mā bhair nāsti bhayaṃ tava evam uktvā tato 'paśyat keśinaṃ sthitam agrataḥ
english: Puraṃdara said to her: "Do not be afraid; you have nothing to fear." Having spoken thus, he then saw Keśin standing before him.

sanskrit: kirīṭinaṃ gadāpāṇiṃ dhātumantam ivācalam haste gṛhītvā tāṃ kanyām athainaṃ vāsavo 'bravīt
english: Wearing a diadem, mace in hand, like a mountain rich with ores — he was holding the maiden by the arm. Then Vāsava spoke to him.

sanskrit: anāryakarman kasmāt tvam imāṃ kanyāṃ jihīrṣasi vajriṇaṃ māṃ vijānīhi viramāsyāḥ prabādhanāt
english: "Why do you, who do the deeds of the ignoble, seek to carry off this maiden? Know me to be the bearer of the thunderbolt — desist from tormenting her!"

sanskrit: keśy uvāca visṛjasva tvam evaināṃ śakraiṣā prārthitā mayā kṣamaṃ te jīvato gantuṃ svapuraṃ pākaśāsana
english: Keśin said: "You, Śakra, should let her go — she has been desired by me. It would be wise for you, still living, to go back to your own city, O Pākaśāsana."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam uktvā gadāṃ keśī cikṣependravadhāya vai tām āpatantīṃ ciccheda madhye vajreṇa vāsavaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having spoken thus, Keśin hurled his mace intending to kill Indra; but Vāsava cut it in two in the middle with his thunderbolt as it came flying at him.

sanskrit: athāsya śailaśikharaṃ keśī kruddho vyavāsṛjat tad āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya śailaśṛṅgaṃ śatakratuḥ bibheda rājan vajreṇa bhuvi tan nipapāta ha
english: Then Keśin, enraged, hurled a mountain peak at him; but Śatakratu, watching it as it flew toward him, shattered that mountain crag with his thunderbolt, O king, and it fell to the ground.

sanskrit: patatā tu tadā keśī tena śṛṅgeṇa tāḍitaḥ hitvā kanyāṃ mahābhāgāṃ prādravad bhṛśapīḍitaḥ
english: But as it fell, Keśin was struck by that very crag; and sorely wounded, he abandoned the illustrious maiden and fled.

sanskrit: apayāte 'sure tasmiṃs tāṃ kanyāṃ vāsavo 'bravīt kāsi kasyāsi kiṃ ceha kuruṣe tvaṃ śubhānane
english: When that demon had departed, Vāsava said to the maiden: "Who are you? Whose are you? And what are you doing here, O fair-faced one?"

sanskrit: kanyovāca ahaṃ prajāpateḥ kanyā devaseneti viśrutā bhaginī daityasenā me sā pūrvaṃ keśinā hṛtā
english: The maiden said: "I am the daughter of Prajāpati, known by the name Devasenā; my sister Daityasenā was previously abducted by Keśin."

sanskrit: sahaivāvāṃ bhaginyau tu sakhībhiḥ saha mānasam āgacchāveha ratyartham anujñāpya prajāpatim
english: "We two sisters came together with our companions to the Mānasa lake for pleasure, having taken leave of Prajāpati."

sanskrit: nityaṃ cāvāṃ prārthayate hartuṃ keśī mahāsuraḥ icchaty enaṃ daityasenā na tv ahaṃ pākaśāsana
english: "And the great demon Keśin always desires to carry off both of us; Daityasenā wishes him as a husband, but I do not, O Pākaśāsana."

sanskrit: sā hṛtā tena bhagavan muktāhaṃ tvadbalena tu tvayā devendra nirdiṣṭaṃ patim icchāmi durjayam
english: "She has been carried off by him, O blessed one, while I have been freed by your strength. O Devendra, I desire the husband you shall appoint for me — one who is invincible."

sanskrit: indra uvāca mama mātṛṣvaseyā tvaṃ mātā dākṣāyaṇī mama ākhyātaṃ tv aham icchāmi svayam ātmabalaṃ tvayā
english: Indra said: "You are the niece of my mother, the daughter of Dakṣa's daughter. But I wish you yourself to declare your own inherent power."

sanskrit: kanyovāca abalāhaṃ mahābāho patis tu balavān mama varadānāt pitur bhāvī surāsuranamaskṛtaḥ
english: The maiden said: "I myself am without power, O mighty-armed one, but my husband shall be powerful; by the boon of my father he will come to be, and he will be bowed to by both gods and demons."

sanskrit: indra uvāca kīdṛśaṃ vai balaṃ devi patyus tava bhaviṣyati etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ tava vākyam anindite
english: Indra said: "What manner of power, O goddess, will your husband possess? I wish to hear this from your own words, O blameless one."

sanskrit: kanyovāca devadānavayakṣāṇāṃ kiṃnaroragarakṣasām jetā sa dṛṣṭo duṣṭānāṃ mahāvīryo mahābalaḥ
english: The maiden said: "He is seen as the conqueror of gods, demons, yakṣas, kiṃnaras, nāgas, and rākṣasas, and of all the wicked — great in heroism and great in strength."

sanskrit: yas tu sarvāṇi bhūtāni tvayā saha vijeṣyati sa hi me bhavitā bhartā brahmaṇyaḥ kīrtivardhanaḥ
english: "He who shall conquer all beings together with you — he shall indeed be my husband, devoted to brahmin virtues and the increaser of glory."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca indras tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā duḥkhito 'cintayad bhṛśam asyā devyāḥ patir nāsti yādṛśaṃ saṃprabhāṣate
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Hearing her words, Indra was troubled and brooded deeply: "There is no one who possesses the qualities this goddess speaks of."

sanskrit: athāpaśyat sa udaye bhāskaraṃ bhāskaradyutiḥ somaṃ caiva mahābhāgaṃ viśamānaṃ divākaram
english: Then he whose radiance rivals the sun's beheld the sun rising, and the glorious moon as well, entering the sun.

sanskrit: amāvāsyāṃ saṃpravṛttaṃ muhūrtaṃ raudram eva ca devāsuraṃ ca saṃgrāmaṃ so 'paśyad udaye girau
english: He saw the auspicious new-moon moment arriving, and the raudra muhūrta as well, and the battle between gods and demons at the rising mountain.

sanskrit: lohitaiś ca ghanair yuktāṃ pūrvāṃ saṃdhyāṃ śatakratuḥ apaśyal lohitodaṃ ca bhagavān varuṇālayam
english: Śatakratu, the blessed one, beheld the eastern dawn filled with reddish clouds, and the ocean — Varuṇa's abode — flushed red with their reflection.

sanskrit: bhṛgubhiś cāṅgirobhiś ca hutaṃ mantraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ havyaṃ gṛhītvā vahniṃ ca praviśantaṃ divākaram
english: He saw the oblation offered with diverse sacred formulas by the Bhṛgus and the Aṅgirases, and fire himself, bearing the oblation, entering the sun.

sanskrit: parva caiva caturviṃśaṃ tadā sūryam upasthitam tathā dharmagataṃ raudraṃ somaṃ sūryagataṃ ca tam
english: He saw the twenty-fourth lunar phase approaching the sun, and likewise the moon — in the path of dharma, in the raudra aspect — having entered the sun.

sanskrit: samālokyaikatām eva śaśino bhāskarasya ca samavāyaṃ tu taṃ raudraṃ dṛṣṭvā śakro vyacintayat
english: Beholding the perfect union of the moon and the sun, and seeing that fierce conjunction, Śakra fell into deep thought.
